hawkish.text: UK CPI inflation increased to 3.1% in August and is likely to rise further over coming quarters.

Overall, the Committee judges that the risks to the inflation outlook are tilted to the upside, and more so than at the time of the July Monetary Policy Report, although there remains scope for the outlook to change materially as events in the Middle East unfold.
However, the risk of such effects, against which policy needs to lean, is greater the longer higher energy prices persist or are more volatile.
At this meeting, the MPC also voted unanimously to reduce the stock of UK government bond purchases held for monetary policy purposes, and financed by the issuance of central bank reserves, to zero.
Three members voted to increase Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points, to 4%.

dovish.text: There has been little evidence so far of material second-round effects in price and wage-setting.

Activity has been slightly stronger than expected, although soft labour market conditions, and the higher interest rates faced by households and businesses since the conflict began, will act to reduce inflation over time.

rows.text: Three members voted to increase Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points, to 4%.
Protracted conflict in the Middle East has contributed to further increases in crude and refined energy prices since the previous meeting, which remain more volatile and higher than pre-conflict.
rows.prev_text: In response to events in the Middle East, crude and refined energy prices have remained volatile and higher than pre-conflict.

rows.text: UK CPI inflation increased to 3.1% in August and is likely to rise further over coming quarters.
Monetary policy is being set to ensure inflation comes down to 2% sustainably as the economy adjusts to the energy shock.
The policy stance required to achieve this will depend on the scale and duration of the shock and how it propagates through the economy.
rows.prev_text: The policy stance required to achieve this will depend on the scale and duration of the shock, and how it propagates through the economy including via financial conditions.

rows.text: There has been little evidence so far of material second-round effects in price and wage-setting.
rows.prev_text: The risk of material second-round effects in price and wage-setting, against which policy needs to lean, is greater the longer higher energy prices persist.

rows.text: However, the risk of such effects, against which policy needs to lean, is greater the longer higher energy prices persist or are more volatile.

Activity has been slightly stronger than expected, although soft labour market conditions, and the higher interest rates faced by households and businesses since the conflict began, will act to reduce inflation over time.
rows.prev_text: Loose labour market conditions, and higher interest rates faced by households and businesses than prior to the conflict, will also act to reduce inflation over time.

rows.text: Overall, the Committee judges that the risks to the inflation outlook are tilted to the upside, and more so than at the time of the July Monetary Policy Report, although there remains scope for the outlook to change materially as events in the Middle East unfold.
rows.prev_text: The Committee judges that the risks to the inflation outlook are tilted to the upside relative to the central projection in the July Monetary Policy Report, but there remains scope for the outlook to change materially as events in the Middle East unfold.

rows.text: The Committee judges that it is appropriate to maintain Bank Rate at this meeting.
The Committee stands ready to act as necessary to ensure that CPI inflation remains on track to meet the 2% target in the medium term.
At this meeting, the MPC also voted unanimously to reduce the stock of UK government bond purchases held for monetary policy purposes, and financed by the issuance of central bank reserves, to zero.

This will be conducted through a multi-year plan, such that the remaining stock is unwound at an annual average pace of £46 billion by the end of 2034, through annual sales of £20 billion alongside maturing gilts.
The impact of the energy shock on the UK economy remains uncertain.
Monetary policy cannot influence energy prices but is being set to ensure that the economic adjustment to them occurs in a way that achieves the 2% inflation target sustainably.
CPI inflation has fallen to 2.6% since the previous meeting, although it is expected to rise later this year as the effects of higher energy prices continue to pass through.
There is little evidence so far to suggest such effects, and there have continued to be clear signs of underlying disinflation in recent data.
